r.정치 구도: Power is heavily concentrated in the presidency, and the military carries great weight in both politics and the economy. Protests in 2011 forced out a president who had ruled for nearly 30 years; in 2012 a candidate from the Muslim Brotherhood won the presidency at the ballot box, but the army removed him the following year. The Brotherhood was then designated a terrorist organization and banned, and critical media and the opposition were sharply curtailed. Constitutional amendments in 2019 lengthened the presidential term to six years and wrote into the constitution a role for the military as guardian of the constitution and the state. Parties loyal to the government swept the parliamentary elections held from late 2025 into early 2026. Rising prices, heavy public debt and the squeeze on household budgets are the government's biggest burdens.

t.why: The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, cutting the sea route between Asia and Europe dramatically. So when Yemen's Houthi rebels began attacking ships in the Red Sea in late 2023, many vessels diverted around the southern tip of Africa and Egypt's canal earnings fell steeply. In 1979 it became the first Arab country to sign a peace treaty with Israel, and it shares a border with Gaza, which makes it a mediator that can talk to both Israel and Hamas. In October 2025 it hosted a summit on ending the Gaza war in the Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh. Because it depends on the Nile for nearly all its water, it protested to the UN Security Council when Ethiopia completed a giant dam upstream in September 2025, calling it a unilateral act. As the Arab world's most populous country, heavily backed by the United States and the Gulf states, its importance grows whenever the Middle East is shaken.
t.rel: The most populous Arab country, with the Suez Canal. It signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1979 and mediates in Gaza talks. It is at odds with Ethiopia over its Nile dam.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in April 1995. Samsung Electronics runs a factory in Beni Suef, south of Cairo, making televisions, tablets and smartphones. With support from KOICA, Korea's development agency, a technological university opened in the same area in 2019 to train skilled workers for local industry. In 2022 Hanwha signed a deal to co-produce K9 self-propelled howitzers with Egypt, expanding defense ties. During the Egyptian president's state visit to Korea in October 2026, the two countries upgraded relations to a strategic partnership and launched negotiations on a CEPA.
t.know: Evidence from their tombs shows the pyramid builders were paid workers, not slaves.
etext: Suez Canal tolls, tourism, remittances from workers abroad and natural gas bring in foreign currency. The pyramids and Red Sea resorts draw a steady flow of visitors, and the many Egyptians working in the Gulf send large sums home. All four, though, swing with events beyond Egypt's control, as the sharp fall in canal revenue during the attacks on Red Sea shipping showed.

A giant gas field discovered in the Mediterranean in 2015 briefly turned it into an exporter, but output has fallen while domestic demand has grown, so since 2024 it has again been importing large amounts of liquefied natural gas. Power shortages brought frequent blackouts in the summer.
The state's and the army's share

The military and state-owned companies run businesses in everything from construction and food to cement and fuel. Critics say they enjoy tax and regulatory advantages, and the IMF has pressed Egypt to sell stakes in state firms and give private companies a level playing field.

With more than 100 million people, it is one of the world's biggest wheat importers, so rising grain prices hit it immediately. Interest on public debt takes up a large share of the budget, and when it let the exchange rate float in March 2024 the Egyptian pound lost much of its value. That same year a UAE sovereign wealth fund agreed to invest 35 billion dollars in developing a stretch of the Mediterranean coast, easing the most urgent shortage of foreign currency.
